nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $s$ (the starting position), a fuel $f$ and a list $c$ of natural numbers (the current circle), the simulation returns the empty list when $f = 0$ or $c$ is empty. Otherwise, with $L$ the length of $c$ and $i = (s + k - 1) \bmod L$, where the subtraction is truncated at $0$, it returns the entry of $c$ at zero-based position $i$ followed by the result of the simulation with the same $k$,…
nodes.title: Fuel-bounded Josephus simulation

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 1$, the Josephus elimination order with step $k$ on the circle $1, \dots, n$ is nonempty and its last entry is $J_k(n)$, the value at $n$ of the Josephus function for elimination step $k$.
nodes.title: The survivor is the last entry of the Josephus elimination order

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the Josephus elimination order with step $k$ on the circle $1, \dots, n$ has exactly $n$ entries.
nodes.title: Length of the Josephus elimination order

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the Josephus elimination order with step $k$ on the circle $1, \dots, n$ is a permutation of the list $1, 2, \dots, n$; in particular, each of $1, \dots, n$ occurs in it exactly once.
nodes.title: The Josephus elimination order is a permutation of the circle

nodes.summary: The Josephus elimination order with step $3$ on the circle $1, \dots, 10$ is $3, 6, 9, 2, 7, 1, 8, 5, 10, 4$: the entries are removed in the order $3, 6, 9, 2, 7, 1, 8, 5, 10$, and the survivor $4$ comes last.
nodes.title: Josephus elimination order for ten people and step three

nodes.summary: The Josephus elimination order with step $2$ on the circle $1, 2, 3$ is $2, 1, 3$: the entry $2$ is removed first, then the entry $1$, and the survivor $3$ comes last.
nodes.title: Josephus elimination order for three people and step two

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, place $1, \dots, n$ in order on a circle and repeatedly remove one entry. When $L$ entries remain and the current position is $s$ (zero-based, initially $s = 0$), the entry at zero-based position $i = (s + k - 1) \bmod L$ is removed, where the subtraction is truncated at $0$, and $i$ becomes the current position, so the next count starts at the entry after the removed one. nodes.title: Josephus elimination order

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ and $n \ge 2$ be natural numbers, let $h_k(x) = x + \lfloor x/(k-1) \rfloor + 1$ for natural numbers $x$, and write $h_k^p$ for the $p$-th iterate of $h_k$. Then there is a natural number $p \ge 1$ with $h_k^{p-1}(k-1) < n(k-1) \le h_k^p(k-1)$ and $J_k(n) = nk - h_k^p(k-1)$, where $J_k$ is the Josephus function for elimination step $k$.
nodes.title: Josephus survivor via the shifted iteration

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ and $n \ge 2$ be natural numbers, let $h_k(x) = x + \lfloor x/(k-1) \rfloor + 1$ for natural numbers $x$, write $h_k^p$ for the $p$-th iterate of $h_k$, and define the real numbers $v = \log n / (\log k - \log(k-1))$ and $w = (\log(n+1) - \log 2) / (\log k - \log(k-1))$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm. Then there is a natural number $p \ge 1$ with $\lfloor w \rfloor \le p \le \lceil v \rceil$…
nodes.title: Logarithmic bounds for the Josephus iteration count

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ and $n \ge 1$ be natural numbers, let $h_k(x) = x + \lfloor x/(k-1) \rfloor + 1$ for natural numbers $x$, and write $h_k^p$ for the $p$-th iterate of $h_k$. Then there is a natural number $p \ge 1$ with $h_k^{p-1}(0) < n(k-1) \le h_k^p(0)$ and $J_k(n) = nk - h_k^p(0)$, where $J_k$ is the Josephus function for elimination step $k$.
nodes.title: Josephus survivor via iteration from zero

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ and $1 \le m \le n$. Write $o_n(m)$ for the position, counting from $1$, at which $m$ appears in the Josephus elimination order of the circle $1, \dots, n$ in which every $k$-th person is removed and the survivor is listed last, and write $G$ for the Grundy number of Maximum Nim with rule function $f(y) = \lfloor y/k \rfloor$. Then $n - o_n(m) = G(nk - m)$.
nodes.title: Josephus elimination positions as Maximum Nim Grundy numbers

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a rule function and let $x$ be a pile size. The position $x$ of the Maximum Nim game with rule $f$ is a P-position if and only if, for every $u$ with $1 \le u \le \min(f(x), x)$, the position $x - u$ is not a P-position.
nodes.title: P-positions of Maximum Nim

nodes.summary: For a rule function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the Maximum Nim game with rule $f$ is the impartial game whose positions are the pile sizes $x \in \mathbb{N}$, in which the moves from $x$ go to $x - u$ for each $u$ with $1 \le u \le \min(f(x), x)$. The rank of a position is the pile size itself, and the starting position is the empty pile $0$.
nodes.title: The Maximum Nim game

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ and let $G$ be the Grundy number of Maximum Nim with rule function $f(y) = \lfloor y/k \rfloor$. Every positive multiple $x$ of $k$ satisfies $G(x) = x/k$.
nodes.title: Maximum Nim Grundy numbers at multiples of the divisor

nodes.summary: In Maximum Nim with rule function $f(x) = \lfloor x/2 \rfloor$, a pile of $5$ stones has Grundy number $1$.
nodes.title: Grundy number of a pile of five in halving Maximum Nim

nodes.summary: In Maximum Nim with rule function $f(x) = \lfloor x/2 \rfloor$, a pile of $4$ stones has Grundy number $2$.
nodes.title: Grundy number of a pile of four in halving Maximum Nim

nodes.summary: In Maximum Nim with rule function $f(x) = \lfloor x/2 \rfloor$, a pile of $3$ stones has Grundy number $0$.
nodes.title: Grundy number of a pile of three in halving Maximum Nim

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ and let $G$ be the Grundy number of Maximum Nim with rule function $f(y) = \lfloor y/k \rfloor$. If $x$ is a natural number not divisible by $k$, then $G(x) = G(\lfloor (k-1)x/k \rfloor)$.
nodes.title: Maximum Nim Grundy numbers at non-multiples of the divisor

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $f(0) = 0$ and $f(m-1) \le f(m) \le f(m-1) + 1$ for every $m \ge 1$, and let $G$ be the Grundy number of Maximum Nim with rule function $f$. If $x \ge 1$ and $f(x-1) < f(x)$, then $G(x) = f(x)$.
nodes.title: Grundy number where the rule function increases

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $f(0) = 0$ and $f(m-1) \le f(m) \le f(m-1) + 1$ for every $m \ge 1$, and let $G$ be the Grundy number of Maximum Nim with rule function $f$. If $x \ge 1$ and $f(x) = f(x-1)$, then $G(x) = G(x - f(x) - 1)$.
nodes.title: Grundy number where the rule function is flat

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $f(0) = 0$ and $f(m-1) \le f(m) \le f(m-1) + 1$ for every $m \ge 1$. Then for every pile size $x \in \mathbb{N}$, the Grundy number of $x$ in Maximum Nim with rule function $f$ is $0$ if and only if $x$ is a P-position (a previous-player win under normal play) of that game.
nodes.title: Grundy value zero characterizes P-positions in Maximum Nim

nodes.summary: For every rule function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and every pile size $x \in \mathbb{N}$, the Grundy number $G_f(x)$ of a pile of $x$ stones in Maximum Nim with rule function $f$ equals the mex (least natural number not in the set) of $\{G_f(x - u) : 1 \le u \le \min(f(x), x)\}$.
nodes.title: Recursive formula for Maximum Nim Grundy numbers

Then for every natural number $i$ with $1 \le i \le n$,
nodes.title: Floor-rule Maximum Nim: one-step Grundy reduction when k = nt + h

Write $G(x)$ for the Grundy number of a pile of $x$ stones in Maximum Nim with rule function $f(y) = \lfloor y/k \rfloor$, let $F(x) = \lfloor (k-1)x/k \rfloor$, and let $F^t$ be the $t$-fold iterate of $F$. Write $G(x)$ for the Grundy number of a pile of $x$ stones in Maximum Nim with rule function $f(y) = \lfloor y/k \rfloor$, let $F(x) = \lfloor (k-1)x/k \rfloor$, and let $F^{t+1}$ be the $(t+1)$-fold iterate of $F$. nodes.title: Floor-rule Maximum Nim: (t+1)-step Grundy reduction when k = nt + h

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 2$ and every natural number $j$ with $1 \le j \le k$, a pile of $k - j$ stones has Grundy number $0$ in Maximum Nim with rule function $f(y) = \lfloor y/k \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Floor-rule Maximum Nim: positions below k have Grundy number zero

nodes.summary: For a rule function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the Grundy number $G_f(x)$ of a pile of $x$ stones in Maximum Nim is defined by recursion on $x$ as the mex (least natural number not in the set) of $\{G_f(x - u) : 1 \le u \le \min(f(x), x)\}$, the Grundy numbers of the positions reachable from $x$ by removing $u$ stones.
nodes.title: Grundy numbers of Maximum Nim

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural number, let $h_k(x) = x + \lfloor x/(k-1) \rfloor + 1$ on natural numbers, and define the real maps $h_k^-(x) = x + \frac{x}{k-1}$ and $h_k^+(x) = x + \frac{x}{k-1} + 1$. nodes.title: Logarithmic bounds on the iterates of h_k

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural number and let $h_k$ be the map $x \mapsto x + \lfloor x/(k-1) \rfloor + 1$ on the natural numbers. For every natural number $x_0$, the iterates $h_k^p(x_0)$ tend to infinity as $p \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Iterates of the Maximum Nim map $h_k$ tend to infinity

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural number and let $h_k$ be the map $x \mapsto x + \lfloor x/(k-1) \rfloor + 1$ on the natural numbers. For all natural numbers $x$ and $x'$ with $x < x'$, we have $h_k(x) < h_k(x')$.
nodes.title: The Maximum Nim map $h_k$ is strictly increasing

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural number and let $h_k$ be the map $x \mapsto x + \lfloor x/(k-1) \rfloor + 1$ on the natural numbers. Every natural number $x$ satisfies $x < x + 1 \le h_k(x)$.
nodes.title: The Maximum Nim map $h_k$ exceeds its argument

nodes.summary: For the map $h_k(x) = x + \lfloor x/(k-1) \rfloor + 1$ on the natural numbers, we have $h_3(2) = 4$.
nodes.title: The value $h_3(2) = 4$ of the Maximum Nim map

nodes.summary: For the map $h_k(x) = x + \lfloor x/(k-1) \rfloor + 1$ on the natural numbers, we have $h_3(0) = 1$.
nodes.title: The value $h_3(0) = 1$ of the Maximum Nim map

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $x$, let $h_k(x) = x + \lfloor x/(k-1) \rfloor + 1$. The paper takes $k \ge 2$; for $k \le 1$ the definition gives $h_k(x) = x + 1$, because $k - 1$ is truncated to $0$ and $\lfloor x/0 \rfloor$ is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: The Maximum Nim map $h_k$

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a finite set of natural numbers and $m$ a natural number. Then $\operatorname{mex}(s)$, the least natural number not in $s$, equals $m$ if and only if $m \notin s$ and every natural number $n < m$ lies in $s$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the minimum excludant

nodes.summary: For a finite set $s$ of natural numbers, $\operatorname{mex}(s)$ is the least natural number that does not belong to $s$.
nodes.title: Minimum excludant of a finite set

nodes.summary: Let $k, n, t, h, s, i$ be natural numbers with $h \ge 1$, $k = nt + h$, $h \le n$ and $s < t$. If $1 \le i \le n$, then $k$ does not divide $n(k - s) - i$.
nodes.title: A Maximum Nim non-divisibility lemma for $s < t$

nodes.summary: Let $k, n, t, h, i$ be natural numbers with $t \ge 1$, $h \ge 1$, $k = nt + h$ and $h \le n$. If $1 \le i \le n$ and $i \ne h$, then $k$ does not divide $n(k - t) - i$.
nodes.title: A Maximum Nim non-divisibility lemma for $i \ne h$

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ and $x$ be natural numbers such that $x$ is not a multiple of $k$. Then $x - \lfloor x/k \rfloor - 1 = \lfloor (k-1)x/k \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Floor identity for non-multiples in Maximum Nim
